title: Accepting QR code payments: A guide for businesses in the UAE
summary: This guide walks you through how to accept QR code payments, how it works, and how to easily set up QR codes in a UAE-based payment app like Ziina.

Imagine you’re at a busy weekend market in Dubai: a queue is starting to form, your customers are ready to pay, but you can only serve one person at a time.


That's where QR code payments can help. By adding a QR stand to your stall, customers can skip the queue by paying another way. All they have to do is scan the code with their phone, authorize the payment, and that’s it – they’ve checked out in seconds.


But how do you actually set up QR code payments? And can you do it without adding another piece of software to your workflow?


In this guide, we'll show you how to set up QR code payments for your UAE business, explain how they work, and answer some of the most common questions about getting started.


We’ll cover:


- How do QR codes work?


- Are QR code payments safe to use?


- How to accept payments using a QR code


- How Ziina can help you accept QR code payments

[Get started today](https://ziina.app.link/webBlog)


## How do QR codes work?


A QR code (short for Quick Response code) is a barcode that stores links, text, or images in a pattern of black and white squares.


If you scan the code with your phone, the camera reads the pattern and instantly displays the encoded content – whether that’s taking you to a webpage, pulling up a restaurant menu, or prompting you to check out right on your screen.


Note:


QR codes often include ‘error correction’ features, which just means that they can often still be scanned even if part of the code is scratched, dirty, or partially covered. The square markers in the corners help the phone recognize the code quickly, even if it's tilted or viewed from an angle.

## QR codes in practice


- Contractors, pop-up sellers, and market vendors that can bring a portable QR stand to a new site and reduce the amount of time customers spend waiting in a queue.

- Vacation rentals and apartments that can display a QR code for guests in case they request additional services such as cleaning or maintenance during their stay.

## Are QR code payments safe to use?


Yes, QR code payments are generally very safe if you’re using a trusted payment provider.


Reputable providers make sure that every transaction is secure. Their advanced fraud protection measures might include PCI-DSS compliance, strong data encryption, tokenization, and real-time fraud monitoring to block suspicious activity.


As a merchant, you can also take a few extra steps to help your customers feel confident when paying:


- Display codes securely in your store (for example, you could put them in places inaccessible from the shop floor)


- Print your code directly onto permanent signage rather than using peel-and-stick paper labels (which are easier to tamper with)


- Train staff to watch out for fake sticker overlays and regularly inspect the stand


- Ask customers to check the recipient name and transaction amount before paying
